thread:
Maya: Heads-up — our demand forecast for next weeks marketing push shows a sharp spike in us-west2. p95 stays within SLO but p99 drifts toward ~550ms on longer sequences. We need a concrete headroom plan and admission control approach.

Eli: Do we have a prewarm + burst model? Also can we opportunistically move low-priority batch work to a cheaper dedicated pool for that window? Need the numbers to compare.

Maya: Current baseline prewarm reserve: 120 GPU-hours/day in us-west2. Promo expected add: ~320 GPU-hours over 48h concentrated on afternoon/evening traffic. If we don't change anything queue depth spikes and p99 degrades.

Noor: Quick back-of-envelope: baseline batching throughput ~180 reqs/s per GPU at median seq=512. Promo traffic skews to >1k tokens frequent, effective throughput drops ~35%. So holding p99 <700ms requires ~1.6x GPUs unless we throttle.

Eli: Options we should weigh:
1) Temporary capacity increase (cost uplift ~ $8k/day).
2) Soft admission control for low-tier or heavy-seq requests (expected GPU-hour savings ~45% during peak).
3) Reduce batching window to 30ms to favor latency at a throughput cost.

Maya: I prefer option #2 combined with a modest prewarm bump. Proposed: soft-reject free-tier large-model requests with 429+Retry-After and add ~20 GPUs to prewarm pool. That should keep p99 in-range while minimizing emergency spend.

Sam: I can implement a canary admission rule scoped to us-west2. Rollout plan: 5% -> 20% -> 100% over ~4h assuming SLIs are healthy. We need explicit SLI gates: p99 latency (overall and by tier), queue depth, and admit-rate by tier.

Noor: Note on networking: during previous promo we saw inter-AZ egress approach NAT/NLB limits. Spinning up more hosts can cause backpressure at the network layer and inflate tail latencies even when GPU slots are available. We should verify egress headroom before scale-up.

Maya: Ops checklist before 02:00 UTC: 1) bump prewarm +20 GPUs, 2) enable canary admission rule, 3) confirm NAT/NLB egress capacity or file an egress bump. If canary fails within 6h -> auto-disable and page #incidents. OK?

Sam: Canary config (draft):
```
admission_rule:
  name: promo-soft-throttle-2026-03
  match: "tier == 'free' && model in ['redwood-xl','open-13b'] && region == 'us-west2'"
  action: soft_reject
  quota_pct: 40
  rollout_schedule: [5,20,100]
  response: { status: 429, body: 'promo backpressure - retry after' }
```

Eli: Cost roughs: prewarm +20 GPUs =~ $6.7k/day. If throttling prevents full-scale demand we save ~4k/day in GPU-hours during peak window. Net incremental ~2.7k/day for safety vs ~8k/day for full temporary burst — cheaper and lower risk. I'll post a short cost table with expected GPU-hour curves.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: promo-soft-throttle-2026-03 to us-west2 (owner: Sam). ETA 02:00 UTC tomorrow. :rocket:

Sam: Will start canary at 02:00 UTC, add dashboard panels: promo-admit-rate, us-west2-queue-depth, p99-latency-by-tier, nat-egress-util. I'll wire alert rules for p99>700ms or queue-depth spike.

Noor: I'll run a quick NAT + NLB saturation sim against current infra and report whether we need an egress bump pre-deploy.

Maya: Thanks all. Reconvene in this thread after the cost table and network sim. If anything changes overnight, ping with @here.
